body.input: Which cloud and data centre companies opened an office in Norway in 2026?

response.content:
Based on available reporting, the following cloud and data-centre companies established or announced new facilities/offices in Norway during 2026:

### Companies with new Norway presence or expansion announced in 2026

1. **Nscale** (UK-based AI cloud infrastructure firm) — In partnership with Norwegian industrial investor **Aker**, Nscale is building the **Stargate Norway** data centre campus near Narvik (Kvandal), with an initial 230 MW capacity. OpenAI was originally part of the project but withdrew in April 2026; **Microsoft** subsequently expanded its agreement with Nscale to take the full compute capacity at the site, including more than 30,000 Nvidia Rubin GPUs planned for delivery in 2027.

2. **Microsoft** — In addition to the Nscale/Narvik deal, Microsoft announced in June–July 2026 a **new 25 MW data centre in Sandnes** (Stavanger region), purchasing a 64-acre industrial-zoned site for NOK 153.6 million. This supplements Microsoft's existing Norway East cloud region (operational since 2019).

3. **CoreWeave** — Listed among companies with existing and planned data-centre operations in Norway as of 2026.

4. **TikTok** (via **Green Mountain**) — Also identified as having existing and planned data-centre capacity in Norway during 2026.

### Notable context

- As of November 2026, Norway's grid operator **Statnett** has paused new power-capacity reservations for data centres, citing grid-stability risks. Around 800 MW of data centres are currently connected, with an additional 4.2 GW reserved and 9.1 GW in the capacity queue. The moratorium is expected to last until at least August 2027.
- The Norwegian Technology Council reported in October 2026 that foreign companies own approximately 90% of data-centre capacity in the country.

# Microsoft reveals plans for data center in Sandnes, Norway

Will join the Norway East region

Microsoft is expanding its European footprint with a data center in Sandnes, Norway.

The project was revealed by the company on June 30, and will see a data center developed in the Sandnes Municipality, which is part of the Stavanger region. [...] The plot of land the data center will be constructed on spans 64 acres and was purchased for NOK153.6 million from Forusstranda Næringspark and Kvål Næringspark. Located at Kvål in Ganddal, it is already zoned for industrial use.

According to E24, the data center will have 25MW of capacity. Further details about the project have not been provided. [...] Also in Norway, Microsoft has signed an agreement with Nscale to lease access to 30,000 Nvidia Rubin GPUs hosted in a data center in Narvik, northern Norway. That data center is estimated to have 230MW of capacity. The two had a pre-existing contract related to the site, with Microsoft having signed on for $6.2 billion of capacity in September 2025. How much the new agreement is worth has not been shared.

Norway is home to existing and planned data centers from Microsoft, Nscale, TikTok (through Green Mountain), CoreWeave, and others. [...] # Norway halts grid connection applications for new data centers

Seeks to limit rapid buildout while regulation catches up

The Norwegian government has temporarily halted the reservation of connections for new data centers.

The move effectively acts as a moratorium on new grid-connected data center developments until regulations are in place. Projects already connected or already grid-approved are unaffected.

System operator Statnett AS said that the halt is expected to be lifted no later than Aug. 1, 2027.

“We want data centers in Norway, but we can’t have all types of data centers,” Digitalization Minister Torgeir Micaelsen said.

“We must therefore control the growth and ensure that Norway gets the data centers we actually need — those that provide the greatest societal benefit.” [...] Last month, the Norwegian Technology Council published a report that said foreign companies own 90 percent of the data center capacity in Norway. It added that data centers provided few jobs beyond the construction phase, and said that revenue from the digital services run from data centers in Norway rarely ends up in Norway.

“Data centers are a key infrastructure in our society, but with the pace of development we are seeing now, it becomes necessary to ask the question of scope and how we can align policy so that we get the most out of scarce resources," Tore Tennøe, the board's director, said.

The group, which advises the government as an independent body, plans to release a report later this year with recommendations on regulating the data center sector.

On November 9, 2026, the Norwegian government suspended grid connection reservations for new data centers"). The moratorium does not apply to already connected facilities or projects that have received connection approval.

However around 18GW is currently being requested for connection - over a third of the country's peak power demand.
